blocks.text: What to check before you buy

parts.t: North Surrey is in the City of Surrey, so Surrey Zoning Bylaw 12000 applies. Every property has a zone, and you can look up any lot in the City's COSMOS map.
Confirm the zone in COSMOS. Surrey replaced its old RF zones with R3, R4 and R5, and some lots are in Comprehensive Development (CD) zones with their own rules.
Ask the City about permits for any suite, coach house or addition. The BC Building Code permits one secondary suite per house.
Pull the title and read any covenants and easements. Section 219 covenants still apply under the newer housing rules.
Near the river or on a slope, ask whether a development permit area applies.
Read the Form B Information Certificate, the bylaws and the strata minutes.
Read the depreciation report and ask what the strata plans to repair.
Confirm what the strata fees cover and whether any special levies are coming.

blocks.text: How I help North Surrey buyers

parts.t: I start by narrowing the eight sub-areas down to the two or three that fit your commute, budget and home type. Then I check the details that matter for each home: the zone and suite permits for a house, or the strata records for a condo or townhome. I pull the title so we can read the covenants together, and I flag anything that needs a question to the City. All of that happens before you remove subjects, while you can still walk away. 1. What areas are in North Surrey?
In Paragon, North Surrey has eight sub-areas: Bridgeview, Bolivar Heights, Fraser Heights, Royal Heights, Cedar Hills, Whalley, Guildford and Port Kells.
2. Is Surrey City Centre part of North Surrey?
Yes. City Centre sits inside the Whalley sub-area, around the Gateway, Surrey Central and King George SkyTrain stations.
3. Are Fleetwood and Panorama Ridge in North Surrey?
No. Paragon lists Fleetwood and Panorama Ridge in other Surrey sub-areas.
4. Which North Surrey areas are on the SkyTrain?
Whalley has three Expo Line stations, and Bridgeview is close to Scott Road Station. Other areas rely on buses to Guildford Exchange or SkyTrain.
5. Which zoning rules apply in North Surrey?
North Surrey is in the City of Surrey, so Surrey Zoning Bylaw 12000 applies. Check any lot's zone in the City's COSMOS map.
6. Can a North Surrey house have a suite?
The BC Building Code permits one secondary suite per house. A suite only counts if it was built with permits, so ask for the permit history.
7. What should I check before buying a North Surrey condo?
Read the Form B, the bylaws, the strata minutes and the depreciation report, and confirm what the strata fees cover.
